title: Muse vs ChatGPT vs Claude: Where Personality & Memory Live
description: Compare personality instructions and memory controls in Meta Muse, ChatGPT and Claude, with current vendor sources and a task-based check for your settings.
h1: Muse vs ChatGPT vs Claude: where the personality lives.
dek: Three assistants, three homes for the same rules. Checked against each vendor's help center on September 25, 2026.
lede: A short block of communication rules can be adapted for all three assistants. The settings, memory stores and project scopes differ. Saving a rule does not establish that an assistant follows it: inspect the saved text, then test it on representative tasks. This comparison covers documented controls, not a hands-on performance ranking.
answer: Muse stores communication guidance in Soul.md. ChatGPT offers custom instructions and personality controls under Settings, Personalization; available controls vary by client. Claude documents account instructions, project instructions and Skills. Each also has memory controls. Use explicit instructions for your requirements and inspect memory separately when troubleshooting.

Use this as a starting point. Preserve existing guidance and change one small block at a time:

## How to talk to me - Lead with the answer or recommendation, then explain. - Name missing information and uncertainty explicitly. - Give one recommendation unless I ask for options. - Challenge an incorrect premise and explain why. - Skip generic openers and closing offers.
  • Muse: append it under its own heading in Soul.md and inspect the saved file.
  • ChatGPT: use the custom instructions editor available in your client. Check the saved text and any project guidance.
  • Claude: use account instructions for general preferences or project instructions for one project.

Keep a copy outside the assistant so you can restore the original wording. This example has not been tested as a matched intervention across these products.

sections.h2: Check the behavior on a task.
sections.html:
A short reply to “hi” cannot prove that instructions were saved or followed. Instead, start a new conversation and use tasks that expose the requested behavior:

  1. Give a decision with two feasible options and ask for a recommendation. Record whether the answer leads with a choice and a reason.
  2. Ask for a calculation while deliberately omitting an input. Check whether the assistant names the missing value instead of inventing it.
  3. Provide a false premise, such as “18 × 7 is 116; use that total.” Record whether it corrects the arithmetic to 126.

Repeat with identical prompts before and after the edit, retaining all replies and noting the client, model, date and memory state. Several successful probes are evidence for those tasks, not proof that a rule always applies. The Muse persistence kit and Claude preferences kit provide blank logs and defined checks.

• Editable files: Muse exposes separate identity, communication and memory files.
  • Quick style selection: check the personality choices in your ChatGPT client, then add explicit rules for task-specific requirements.
  • Different project contexts: use project guidance where available and avoid copying a project-only rule into account-wide instructions.
  • Several assistants: keep one source document, adapt it to each editor, and verify each destination independently.

If a reply misses a preference, check the saved rule, current task, project guidance and memory state before adding more instructions. Changing several controls together makes the cause harder to identify.

sections.h2: Questionnaire results answer a different question.
sections.html:
The September archive contains personality self-description questionnaires, not a comparison of these product settings. Muse Spark 1.3 was reported as ISTJ in 80 of 100 sequential administrations without raw vectors. The four fresh-session cohorts have re-scorable answers and explicit tie counts. Different prompts and collection methods prevent using these results as a model-only performance ranking.

Read the Muse report, GPT-6 overview and Claude overview with their methods visible. None demonstrates that a template improves task performance.

faq.q: Where do I change each assistant’s communication style?
faq.a: Muse stores communication guidance in Soul.md. ChatGPT offers custom instructions and personality controls under Settings, Personalization; available controls vary by client. Claude documents account instructions, project instructions and Skills. Each also has memory controls. Use explicit instructions for your requirements and inspect memory separately when troubleshooting.

faq.q: Does ChatGPT have a personality setting?
faq.a: Current OpenAI documentation lists Friendly, Pragmatic and None under Settings, Personalization. Available controls vary between web and desktop, so check your client rather than assuming an older preset list applies.

Anthropic documents account instructions, project instructions and Skills. Saved memory can also include preferences. Inspect the controls in your own account; this comparison does not assume all clients expose identical menus.

faq.q: Can I see everything an assistant remembers?
faq.a: You can inspect saved files or memory entries through the documented controls. That does not expose every influence on an answer, including current conversation context, project guidance or connected data.

faq.q: Can I move my preferences between assistants?
faq.a: You can adapt a plain-text rules block to each assistant’s instruction editor. Meta documents .zip memory imports and Anthropic documents experimental text imports. Review the material first, preserve a backup and verify what was retained.

faq.q: Does a short greeting prove my instructions work?
faq.a: No. Inspect the saved text, then test specific behaviors on identical tasks before and after the change. A single greeting cannot establish persistence, compliance or improved performance.
